title: LVF2: A Statistical Timing Model based on Gaussian Mixture for Yield Estimation and Speed Binning
problem: Liberty Variation Format (LVF), the industrial standard for statistical timing models, uses a single Gaussian distribution that loses accuracy when timing distributions are non-Gaussian due to process variations. This inaccuracy affects yield estimation and speed binning in semiconductor design.
motivation: Process variation is critical for determining semiconductor yield and economic return as transistor sizes scale down to 22nm and beyond.
method: LVF2 replaces the single Gaussian model with two weighted skewed-normal (SN) distributions to capture multi-modal timing distributions more accurately. The approach maintains backward compatibility with LVF while improving non-Gaussian distribution modeling. Validation performed on TSMC 22nm standard cells for both delay and transition time.
key_novelty: Using two weighted skewed-normal distributions instead of a single Gaussian to model non-Gaussian timing distributions in statistical timing analysis.
contributions: Novel LVF2 statistical timing model combining weighted skewed-normal distributions with LVF backward compatibility
7.74X binning error reduction in delay and 9.56X in transition time compared to LVF
4.79X and 7.18X reduction in 3σ-yield error for delay and transition time respectively
Practical validation on TSMC 22nm technology standard cells

metrics.accuracy: 7.74X binning error reduction (delay), 9.56X (transition time); 4.79X 3σ-yield error reduction (delay), 7.18X (transition time); 2X path delay error reduction

limitations: Error reduction for path delay diminishes due to Central Limit Theorem effects when combining multiple gate delays, though 2X improvement still achieved for typical 8-inverter paths.
primary_theme: Statistical timing model for improved yield estimation
